items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Paul went to New York with Luis Russell after King Oliver’s band broke up... He said, 'You play as much as that cat in the band we got.' Luis Russell’s band.

ctx.x: So you had a banjo-uke first.

Yeah. That’s how I started with the music business. Joe Presser’s son, ’round the corner, who was my good friend, he could blow a kazoo. He was interested in Kid Rena. He knew Kid Rena’s riffs. He knew Buddy Petit’s riffs, Chris Kelly’s riffs. He had that kind of mind. He was destined to become a musician, but he never was. He come around, we standing on the corner, he start playing this . . . I start playing the ukulele Ain’t Gonna Rain No More and et cetera, and he fell in, and he starts singing while I was…
What kind of stuff did y’all play? What songs?

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: Pops Foster was with Luis Russell

ctx.x: Yeah, he was with Chick Webb. They wanted somewhere to jam and play, so Harry would put them on. Sometimes we'd go to work at ten o'clock, and see half-a-dozen musicians there with their horns. They wanted to play, and also at the same time make auditions.

Harry was a wonderful musician. He was an arranger. He arranged some things that Duke used. And he and I... He just liked me. So later on he asked me... Albert Morgan had come through and made a splash on the bass, and Pops Foster was with Luis Russell, and everybody was taking lessons from him. They couldn't get to Braud, because Braud was doubling with Duke, playing theatres and the Cotton Club. And he asked me, said, "Man, that's a helluva bass. Have they got any more down there like that?" I said, "Yeah." I…
